questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to use a telephone politely
Why British people don't like hugs
Why greetings matter and where 'hello' comes from
How diplomats learn foreign languages
questions.why: Catherine says they're exploring the world of greetings and the history of 'hello'.

questions.q: What does Catherine advise about kissing someone as a greeting?
options: Always kiss twice
Kiss the air close to the cheek
Never kiss anyone
Kiss only people you know well, and only once
questions.why: She says 'definitely an air-kiss! Close to the cheek, but don't touch.'

questions.q: According to Andy Scott, why are greetings so important?
options: They show our relationships and intentions
They show other people how well educated and polite we are
They help us remember people's names
They are required by law in some countries
questions.why: He says through greetings we reaffirm or test our bonds and signal our intentions.

questions.q: Why might someone give a hug instead of a handshake?
options: Because they are cold
Because they forgot the rules
Because handshakes are rude
To test whether a friendship has grown
questions.why: Rob says we might check if our friendship has grown by offering something warmer, like a hug.

questions.q: What does Scott suggest if you get a greeting wrong?
options: Just laugh about it
Apologise many times
Start again
Leave quickly
questions.why: Catherine says greetings also reduce tension, 'So if you get it wrong, just laugh about it.'

questions.q: According to Dr Laura Wright, how was 'hello' first used?
options: As a polite greeting to friends
As a way to say goodbye
As a shout to someone far away
As a word in letters
questions.why: She says 'It starts as a distant hailing', yelling at someone miles away.

questions.q: What made 'hello' become a common greeting?
options: A famous book about good manners
The invention of the telephone
The first radio programmes
School lessons
questions.why: She says 'It's not until the invention of telephones we really get to use hello as a greeting'.

questions.q: Why did people first say 'hello' on the telephone?
options: To be polite to the operator who connected the call for them
Because it was the law
To end the call
To get attention while waiting to be connected
questions.why: She says it was 'an attention-grabbing device', for example to attract the operator's attention.
